Dev Containers and Devbox make sure every developer on a team has the same programs and versions installed (the same toolchain). Flisk runs the app's services, the parts of your app; it checks your tools but does not install them.

| | Dev Containers | Devbox | Flisk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Installs the toolchain (Node, Go, CLIs) | Yes (image and features) | Yes (Nix packages) | No (`flisk doctor` checks it) |
| Runs the app's services together | Partial (with a Compose file) | Partial (`devbox services`) | Yes |
| Gateway URL per service | No | No | Yes (Traefik `*.localhost`) |
| Scaffold a new service | No | No | Yes (`flisk resource`) |
| Editor integration | Yes (VS Code, JetBrains, Codespaces) | Partial (generates a devcontainer) | No (any editor) |
| Detects where it runs | n/a | n/a | Yes (`flisk doctor` reports devcontainer, Codespaces, WSL2) |

**Where they are stronger**

- Both solve the classic "works on my machine" problem for the toolchain, which Flisk leaves to you.

**Use them together.** Run Flisk inside a dev container: the container brings the tools, Flisk brings the running stack (your app, up and running).

More: [agent-hosts.md](../agent-hosts.md)

Cells describe each tool's own features as documented; "Partial" means it needs extra setup or covers part of the row. Spotted a mistake? [Open an issue](https://github.com/flisk-sh/flisk/issues/new).
